$Comment: Example FAMILY-GATED VARIANT overlay: 'horrific' stacks on TOP of a base rarity (so you get 'Horrific Epic Spider' = epic base with the horrific premium on it), and rolls ONLY on the spider family (native 'Spiders' NPCGroup, or any role matching 'Spider*' as a fallback). It grants the spider-exclusive 'venomous' affix. Delete this file (and Affixes/Venomous.json) to remove the example. Roll.Chance is this variant's ABSOLUTE spawn probability on an eligible mob (keep the chances of co-occurring variants summing to <= 1). Roll.AllowedRarities gates which BASE rarities it may overlay ('*' = any incl. a plain mob; e.g. ['epic','legendary'] = only on epic+). DifficultyMultiplier is multiplied with the base rarity's own on the difficulty the curve is read at, so keep it modest: 1.25 sits under the entry tier's own step, makes a plain horrific spider about a quarter more dangerous than a plain one, and lifts a Horrific Legendary (2.4 times 1.25) exactly to a Boss's fold and no further. AuraEffectId is a fallback body-tint applied ONLY when the base rarity has no aura (a plain-base horrific spider); a rarity-backed one keeps the rarity aura. Loot is the overlay's OWN death loot, rolled IN ADDITION to whatever the base rarity pays, so this venom table lands on top of the base tier's drops rather than replacing them; Multipliers.Loot multiplies the base tier's pass count.
Name: Horrific
